Area.evidence_source: [/page/5/Text/9] Data analysis identified a multiplicity of risk factors in the lives of the young people who died. In virtually all the case studies, these risk factors occurred in combination. Here they are discussed under three broad headings. The first of these concerns risk factors that were located in the individuals and their behaviour. These include mental health problems, substance misuse, previous suicidal behaviour and talk, self-harm, and perfectionism. The second group of factors focuses on social networks and [/page/6/Text/3] includes students' relationships and the transmission of suicidal behaviour. These are widely recognised risk factors for suicide but they may be heightened in education settings where students are particularly reliant on the network of friendships and contacts which student life offers. The third group includes factors specific to student life including academic progress and transitional periods in the academic year.
